\section{Mixer topologies and design requirements}

The active mixer follows the single-balanced topology shown in Fig.~6.42, and the passive mixer follows the NMOS implementation shown in Fig.~6.15(b). Both core topologies are implemented directly, without changing their circuit structure, in native Virtuoso schematics and simulated with Cadence Spectre through ADE.\footnote{The Cadence schematic and simulation figures were exported in day mode because the default night-mode exports were difficult to read.}

\subsection{Measured comparison}

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{Xrr}
\toprule
Metric & Active & Passive \\
\midrule
Differential voltage gain (dB) & \ensuremath{8.573} & \ensuremath{-5.975} \\
Voltage conversion loss (dB) & \ensuremath{-8.573} & \ensuremath{5.975} \\
Transducer power gain (dB) & \ensuremath{1.584} & \ensuremath{-12.96} \\
Transducer power loss (dB) & \ensuremath{-1.584} & \ensuremath{12.96} \\
Loaded SSB NF (dB) & \ensuremath{11.15} & \ensuremath{16.69} \\
Loaded DSB NF (dB) & \ensuremath{8.124} & \ensuremath{13.71} \\
Input IIP3 (dBm/tone) & \ensuremath{-2.718} & \ensuremath{-5.472} \\
Input P1dB midpoint (dBm) & \ensuremath{-15.55} & \ensuremath{-15.08} \\
Core DC power (mW) & \ensuremath{0.6851} & \ensuremath{0} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}


The active circuit provides \ensuremath{8.573} dB voltage gain and \ensuremath{1.584} dB power gain at \ensuremath{0.6851} mW core power. The passive circuit has \ensuremath{5.975} dB voltage loss and \ensuremath{12.96} dB transducer power loss. Its zero core DC power excludes the ideal external LO driver. Loaded SSB NF is \ensuremath{11.15} / \ensuremath{16.69} dB (active/passive).

The measured IIP3 values are \ensuremath{-2.718} / \ensuremath{-5.472} dBm; active has the higher measured value. Compression and intermodulation are evaluated separately, with the uncertainty/brackets shown below.

The measured input P1dB values are \ensuremath{-15.55} / \ensuremath{-15.08} dBm; passive has the higher measured value. Compression and intermodulation are evaluated separately, with the uncertainty/brackets shown below.
